questions.prompt: SAXPY y[i] = a*x[i] + y[i] on floats: 2 FLOPs, reads x and y, writes y. What's its arithmetic intensity in FLOP/byte? (Round to 3 decimals.)
A GPU has 2,000 GFLOP/s peak and 500 GB/s bandwidth. Where is its ridge point, in FLOP/byte?
On that GPU, a kernel with intensity 1.5 can reach at most how many GFLOP/s?
A memory-bound kernel runs at 90% of peak bandwidth. What's the most promising next step?
options: Reduce DRAM traffic (reuse, fusion, smaller types)
Nothing: it's already at its limit
questions.explanation: At 90% of bandwidth, the only way up is to need fewer bytes, i.e. raise intensity. Faster math doesn't help a memory-bound kernel.

questions.prompt: A new GPU doubles peak FLOP/s but keeps bandwidth the same. What happens to the ridge point?
Which change raises a kernel's arithmetic intensity (as measured with DRAM traffic)?
options: Reusing loaded data from shared memory instead of reloading it
Fusing two kernels so the intermediate never goes to DRAM
Storing data as FP16 instead of FP32
Running at a higher clock speed
questions.explanation: All three cut bytes for the same FLOPs. Clock speed changes the roof, not the kernel's intensity.
